text:
Here are the strongest open-ear options for running, based on the reviews in these results.

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds**
- Runner's World picks these as its overall winner, and WIRED calls them the best clip-on sound. Physical buttons are easy to use mid-run. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)
- Downsides: expensive, IPX4 water resistance, and about 7 hours of battery. Runner's World found them a bit quiet in heavy traffic. WIRED listed the price at $199, down from $299, but sale prices change.

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2**
- Sits on the cheekbones and leaves your ears fully open, which suits busy roads. The bass is much improved over the original model. [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)
- RTINGS rates it as more durable than the Bose, with IP55 and multi-device pairing, though it's a bit less comfortable on the cheekbones. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)
- Downsides: the band can interfere with long hair or winter hats, and it sounds less clear than the older OpenRun. Listed at $180.

**Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2**
- WIRED rates 10 hours per charge and 40 hours with the case, with an IP57 rating. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best for running, Nothing Ear (Open)**
- SoundGuys names these its best running pick, with good bass for an open design, an IP54 rating, and a customizable EQ. Listed at $99 (MSRP $149). [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

**Soundcore AeroFit 2 (good value)**
- Hook-style open earbuds with IP55, about 10 hours per charge (42 with the case), and LDAC on Android. [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2)
- Prices differ between sources. Dealectric lists $129.99 and says code AFSC20 took $25.99 off on 2026-10-22, while SoundGuys lists $79.99 (MSRP $99.99). Check the final price at checkout.
- Buy link: [Soundcore AeroFit 2 at Soundcore's US store](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). This is an affiliate link. Dealectric earns a commission at no extra cost to you, and the code's validity is set by the store's checkout.

**Budget picks**
- JLab Flex Open Earbuds, about $40. Runner's World says they're comfortable and a good low-risk way to try clip-ons, but the sound is basic. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- Soundpeats PearlClip Pro, about $50. WIRED recommends them for trying open earbuds without spending much. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Quick guidance**
- **Clip-on earbuds** (Bose, Shokz OpenDots, AeroFit 2) suit people who want better sound and comfort.
- **Bone conduction** (OpenRun Pro 2) gives the most awareness of traffic.
- Open designs leak sound and block no noise, so keep the volume low enough to hear what's around you.

I don't have verified purchase links for the other products, so I've linked to their reviews instead. Prices and promotions change, so confirm them at checkout.
